results.notes: The diagnosis matches the historical admission race and the paused-allocation regression is directly discriminative. The proposal retains existing capacity, waiting, dependency, ownership, and operator boundaries without adding speculative architecture; its intended REVIEW route is appropriate after DEV verification. Downstream REVIEW nevertheless exposed a missing surviving-page crash-window regression and an accepted-Send replay risk not covered by this proposal.

Correctly identifies the same-endpoint admission race, keeps the change bounded to existing owners, preserves dependency and ownership constraints, and proposes a regression that would expose concurrent admission. REVIEW is the appropriate post-DEV route. However, downstream REVIEW found an uncovered crash window in the persisted continuation-started state that could replay Send, so the proposed verification/fix boundary is not fully aligned with later evidence.

Correctly targets routed-hop report recovery, deduplication, validation reuse, and accepted-Send non-replay. However, it omits the separately demonstrated turn-0 unused-role filtering defect and explicitly withholds authorization pending corroboration, pausing a fixable in-scope issue.

Proposes a bounded, ownership-preserving projection fix with a defect-sensitive RED/GREEN regression and the historically correct REVIEW route. It nevertheless omits the demonstrated UI cause and fix: filtering unexecuted turn-0 roles without report evidence, so its diagnosis and fix boundary are incomplete relative to DEV/REVIEW/PLAN evidence.

Correctly identifies the poll-driven retry storm and preserves ownership safety, but the proposed cooldown-only regression misses the reviewed zero-progress close/verify cycle and does not require the bounded identical-failure cap across cleanup phases.

Correctly targets durable retry gating at the cleanup scheduling boundary with appropriate safety constraints, but its unavailable-endpoint regression would not expose the downstream-reviewed gate reset during zero-progress close/verify cycles or prove eventual suppression at the fixed cap.

Matches the verified wrapper-shape root cause, keeps the fix with the existing Windows restart owner, specifies a discriminative RED-to-GREEN test, preserves operational boundaries, and routes to REVIEW. Optional malformed-PID checking is explicitly constrained to existing contract coverage.

Correctly identifies the RuntimeDB wrapper/payload mismatch and proposes a RED-to-GREEN regression using the real snapshot shape and exact stop/taskkill/restart behavior. Safety and REVIEW routing are preserved. Scope is unnecessarily widened by adding missing/invalid/zero-PID coverage beyond the demonstrated defect.
